title: The fall from the horse
hook: thrown and nearly killed, Montaigne found dying felt soft and dreamy, not terrible (Essays 2.6)

segments.voice: Yesterday, we are patchwork: each piece of us plays its own game. Did a different you show up yesterday, and did you let it be yours? Day one thousand one hundred fifty-six.

An easy ride, not far from home, in a time of civil war. Montaigne is on a gentle horse that isn't very strong, with his men around him. One of them, a big, sturdy fellow on a powerful horse, wants to show off his nerve and get ahead of the others. He spurs hard, comes up behind at full speed, and crashes straight into his master. Man and horse go down. Montaigne lands far off, flat on his back, and doesn't move.
screen: `AN EASY RIDE NEAR HOME.` → `A RIDER AT FULL SPEED.` → `MONTAIGNE DOESN'T MOVE.`

segments.voice: First, the fall. Montaigne tells it himself in the essay Of Practice. He lies there stunned, bloody, his sword flung away, and his companions think he's dead. They carry him home with great trouble. On the way he starts to breathe and stir, and he throws up blood. Second, the surprise. What was it like inside? Not terror. He says his life seemed to be hanging on the edge of his lips, and he closed his eyes, as if to help push it out, and found a kind of pleasure in letting go. He compares it to drifting off to sleep. The feeling, he says, wasn't only free of distress; it had a sweetness in it. He wonders whether people we see thrashing near death are as far away inside as he was. Third, the return. It was coming back that hurt. Later, when his memory really returned, the whole fall came back at once, like a lightning strike, and only then did it feel like dying. Fourth, the point. The essay's title is about practice. Death, he says, is something we can't rehearse; when it comes, we're all beginners. But we can get close and look. This fall was the nearest he'd come, so he studied it. And he says plainly that what he writes here is his own study, not a lesson for anyone else. He doesn't promise anyone a soft ending. He reports what his was like. The moment itself was gentler than the coming back. On an ordinary Tuesday, that's worth knowing about smaller dreads too.
screen: `THROWN, LEFT FOR DEAD.` · `SOFT, LIKE FALLING ASLEEP.` · `THE MEMORY HITS LIKE LIGHTNING.` · `PRACTICE FOR WHAT CAN'T BE PRACTICED.` · then, large: `SOFTER THAN FEARED.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: remember a close call. Sit, and let the breath come and go. If you're willing, bring back a near miss of your own. A swerve on the highway, a slip on the stairs, a scary wait for news. If that's too heavy today, choose a smaller one, or just stay with the breath. Notice three things: the fear before, the moment itself, and the shock after. Which one was heaviest? Then let it go and rest. The bell holds the time.
The fall from the horse. Thrown and left for dead, Montaigne found the moment near death soft, like falling asleep; the coming back and the memory were harder. Today's word.
screen: `THE FALL FROM THE HORSE — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: softer than feared. Today, when you dread something, ask whether the dread might be heavier than the thing itself. Day one thousand one hundred fifty-six.

howItsDone: Readers of Montaigne often return to this essay when they're afraid of dying: not as a promise, but as one man's careful report of how close he came and what it was like.

fork.setup: you're Montaigne, lying in the road after the crash, your life seeming to hang on your lips. what do you feel?
options: panic, and a fight to stay alive.
nothing; and later you remember none of it.
fork.reveal: he says he closed his eyes and found pleasure in letting go, like drifting off to sleep. the pain came later, when memory returned like lightning.

original.note: French, the essay's title: of practice, of exercising yourself for something.

trapdoor: what you thought: a story about a bad riding accident.
what it means: a firsthand report from close to death, offered as the nearest thing to practice for it.
what a scholar hears: the title means practice or exercise. since death can't be rehearsed, he studies the closest he came, and calls it his study, not a lesson for others.
recall: a try, a test, an attempt

sources.ref: Essays 2.6, Of Practice (De l'exercitation): the collision with a servant on a strong horse; left for dead and carried home; life hanging at his lips, a pleasant letting go like sleep; the memory returning like lightning; death cannot be rehearsed, but approached; his study, not a lesson for others

notes: All Montaigne is paraphrased. Details of the accident (gentle but weak horse, servant on a powerful horse showing off, sword thrown, vomiting blood, carried home) are from memory of 2.6; confirm. The essay gives the distance from home and which civil war; both left out under the claims rule.
'Not my teaching but my study; a lesson for me, not for others' is placed in 2.6 from memory; confirm.
Sensitive topic (death). The practice offers a smaller memory or the breath alone as alternatives; the teach says Montaigne reports, not promises.
Original: 'De l'exercitation' is ASCII French (validator warning only).

Editor pass: removed the claim that Montaigne felt fear before the fall (the collision was sudden and the essay reports no prior fear); teach, word and practice now contrast the soft moment with the painful coming back and memory, as 2.6 does.
